subject: Post-call recap: discovery & data privacy requirements (Finexa)
messages:
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Amit Shah <amit.shah@finexa.com>, Priya Rao <priya@finexa.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: discovery & data privacy requirements (Finexa)

Hi Amit & Priya,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Below is a short recap from our discovery so we have alignment on pain points, current stack, success criteria, and next steps. Please reply with corrections or anything I missed.

Summary of pain points:
- Unpredictable latency and cost spikes when using 3rd-party LLM endpoints for customer-facing chat (affects SLAs).
- Need strict PII handling and retention controls for regulatory audits (payments & KYC flows).
- Lack of centralized audit logs to demonstrate data movement and redaction for compliance.

Current stack:
- Product uses a mixture of in-house services + third-party LLMs (shared API keys).
- Auth & logging: internal SSO, logs go to CloudWatch + Splunk; no dedicated PII redaction pipeline.
- Data classification: PII often appears in prompts/requests; review happens manually.

Success criteria for pilot (6–8 weeks):
1) Integrate Redwood Dedicated or Private control plane so we can control keys & network (VPC).
2) Demonstrate PII redaction at inference pipeline (configurable redaction rules + automated redaction).
3) Provide auditable retention settings + exportable audit logs for tokens/requests for compliance team.
4) Keep 95th percentile latency under 300ms for our common request sizes.

Specific privacy/logging requirements we captured:
- PII (names, emails, SSNs, payment tokens) must be redacted at or before persistence. No raw PII stored in long-term logs.
- Retention policy: short-term raw telemetry (30 days), redacted logs retained longer (3 years) for audit.
- We need a signed SOC2 summary + exportable audit logs for procurement.
- Request-level audit trail (who called, model version, input hash, redaction mask) is required.

Proposed next steps:
- I attached a short security overview + our SOC2 summary. Please confirm which controls you need as evidence.
- If you’re open, I’ll set up an intro/tech deep-dive with our CS lead (Laura) and engineers next Wed or Thu.
- I’ll draft a mutual action plan (MAP) with timelines and deliverables and share for review.

Action items (owner):
- Marissa: share security attachments + MAP draft (today) [attached].
- Finexa: confirm retention windows and any additional redaction rules (by Fri).
- Rishi/Laura: prep technical deep-dive materials and SOC2 artefacts.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: Redwood_Security_Overview.pdf; SOC2-Summary-2025.pdf
From: Amit Shah <amit.shah@finexa.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@finexa.com>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 16:25:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: discovery & data privacy requirements (Finexa)

Thanks Marissa — this is very helpful and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Retention windows: we can commit to short-term raw telemetry retention of 30 days, redacted artifacts retained for 36 months. We will need proof that raw PII is not persisted beyond the 30-day window (or is encrypted with customer-managed keys and isolated).
2) Audit logs: procurement needs a way to export per-request audit logs (CSV or JSON) that include input hash, redaction mask, model version, timestamp, and requester id.
3) Redaction: we prefer system-level redaction (server-side) before logs hit Splunk. Client-side redaction is acceptable only if we can verify via hashes and reproducible masking rules.

We’re generally open to Redwood Dedicated or Private depending on cost and deployment time. If Private, we’ll need a deployment checklist for our infra/security team.

Can you confirm Laura can join the tech deep-dive and that we can see examples of the exportable audit logs?

—Amit
Amit Shah
Head of Product (Payments) | Finexa
amit.shah@finexa.com
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Amit Shah <amit.shah@finexa.com>, Priya Rao <priya@finexa.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: discovery & data privacy requirements (Finexa)

Hi Amit — appreciate the clarifications. Quick answers inline: 

- Retention/CMK: We can support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for encryption of persisted telemetry in our Private offering; for Dedicated we offer tenant-isolated storage with encryption-at-rest and recommended key rotation. We will include a deployment checklist for Private in the MAP.

- Audit exports: Yes — we can produce exportable per-request audit logs (JSON/CSV) that include the fields you listed. I’ll attach a sample export (anonymized) to the MAP.

- Redaction: Redwood’s pipeline supports server-side redaction rules (configurable regex & ML-based PII detectors). We can show the redaction mask alongside an input hash so your team can verify raw data isn’t retained.

Next steps I’ll take this morning:
- Share MAP draft: Finexa-MAP-Draft.docx (attached)
- Include sample anonymized audit export (inlined in the MAP)
- Propose tech deep-dive times: Wed 18 Feb or Thu 19 Feb (PST) — please confirm availability.

Laura, Rishi — can you prepare: SOC2 artifacts we can share, a sample audit export (anonymized), and a short runbook for Private deployment checklist?

Thanks,
Marissa

Hi Amit / Priya — Laura from Redwood CS here. Nice to meet you virtually.

I’ve started assembling the SOC2 summary and an anonymized sample audit export. Notes: 
- SOC2 summary covers relevant CC controls for logging, encryption, access control; I’ll redact any org-specific identifiers.
- Sample audit export will be delivered as JSON+CSV and will include: request_id, timestamp, model_version, requester_id (hashed), input_hash, redaction_mask, retention_ttl.
- For deployment, our Private checklist includes steps for VPC peering, CMK setup, and verification of redaction rules in a staging environment.

Proposed MAP items from CS perspective:
- Week 0: Kickoff + scoping call
- Week 1: Technical deep-dive + staging integration
- Week 2–4: Pilot ingest & redaction tuning
- Week 5: Compliance review + export validation
- Week 6–8: Production rollout decision and runbook handoff

I’ll share SOC2 and the sample export after internal review (aiming today). Marissa — I put Wed 18 Feb 10:00 PST as one proposed slot for the deep-dive; does that work for Finexa?

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Customer Success Lead | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Thanks everyone — Wed 18 Feb 10:00 PST works for us. A couple of follow-ups before then:

- Please include an example of the redaction mask format and a short note on how ML-based PII detection handles edge cases (e.g., masked payment tokens, fuzzy names).
- Procurement requests: a formal deployment checklist + high-level cost estimate for Dedicated vs Private (ballpark).
- Can you confirm if Redwood supports on-the-fly token redaction (pre-logging) vs post-hoc redaction only? We prefer pre-logging when possible.

We’ll review the MAP and SOC2 summary once received and aim to provide any additional compliance controls by EOD Monday. Looking forward to the deep-dive.

—Amit
